title: COD Order Confirmation Calls
summary: Call every cash-on-delivery order soon after it is placed, in the customer's language, to confirm items, amount and address, offer a UPI prepaid option and tag the order before it ships.

seo.title: COD Order Confirmation Voice Calls | VipraTech
seo.description: Voice agent that calls cash-on-delivery customers to confirm orders and addresses, offers UPI prepaid conversion and flags risky orders before dispatch.

problem.intro: Cash on delivery remains a large share of orders for many Indian D2C brands, and every refused or undeliverable COD parcel comes back as RTO, paid for in both directions. Calling each order to confirm it is the obvious fix, but calling teams cannot reach every order quickly, especially at night and on sale days.

pain_points.title: RTO costs both ways
pain_points.detail: Refused and undeliverable COD orders incur forward and return shipping, plus inventory stuck in transit.

pain_points.title: Calling teams cannot keep up
pain_points.detail: Manual teams call a fraction of orders, late, and miss night-time and sale-day peaks.

pain_points.title: Incomplete addresses
pain_points.detail: Missing landmarks, wrong pincodes and incomplete house numbers lead to failed delivery attempts.

pain_points.title: Fake and impulse orders
pain_points.detail: Prank orders, duplicate orders and serial refusers are caught only after the parcel has shipped.

solution.overview: We build an outbound voice agent that calls each new COD order shortly after it is placed, in Hindi, English or the customer's regional language. It confirms the items and amount, checks the address, asks for a landmark or corrected pincode where needed, and offers a UPI payment link if you run a prepaid option. Answers update the order in Shopify or your OMS as confirmed, cancelled, address updated or unreachable, with scheduled retries and a WhatsApp fallback. Orders with risk signals, such as a number with past refusals, are flagged for your operations team to decide.
capabilities: Calls new COD orders within your chosen window, with retry schedules and calling-hour limits
Confirms items, quantity and amount, and records cancellation reasons in the customer's words
Checks address completeness and pincode serviceability and collects landmarks or corrections
Sends a UPI payment link through your gateway when the customer chooses to prepay
Tags orders in the OMS as confirmed, cancelled, address updated or unreachable
Flags risk signals such as past refusals, duplicate orders and mismatched pincodes for operations

workflow.title: New COD order
workflow.detail: The OMS sends each new COD order to the calling queue with items, amount and address.

workflow.title: Call the customer
workflow.detail: The agent calls within the agreed window, names the brand and states that the call is recorded.

workflow.title: Confirm order and address
workflow.detail: Items, amount and address are confirmed, and missing landmarks or pincode errors are corrected.

workflow.title: Offer prepaid option
workflow.detail: If you run a prepaid option, the agent offers a UPI link and sends it on WhatsApp or SMS.

workflow.title: Check risk and outcome
workflow.detail: Confirmed, cancelled, unreachable and risky outcomes are tagged; risky orders go to operations.

workflow.title: Update and dispatch
workflow.detail: The OMS is updated, and only confirmed or approved orders move to dispatch.

inputs: New COD orders with items, amount, address and phone number
Pincode serviceability from your courier partners
RTO and refusal history by phone number and pincode
outputs: Order tags: confirmed, cancelled, address updated, unreachable or flagged
UPI payment links sent and prepaid conversions
Daily report linking call outcomes to delivery results
human_in_the_loop: Operations decides on orders flagged for risk, high-value orders and any decision to block a repeat refuser. Address changes are confirmed by the customer on the call or over WhatsApp before the order ships.
integrations: Courier aggregator for serviceability and delivery outcomes
WhatsApp Business API and SMS gateway
guardrails: Calls only within allowed hours, with a capped number of retries
Clear identification of the brand and recording disclosure at the start
No pressure tactics or false urgency when offering prepaid
Payment links only through your official gateway, never card details by voice
Customers can opt out of further calls
compliance_notes: Order confirmation calls are service calls about the customer's own purchase; promotional content is kept out of them so they stay within TRAI commercial-communication rules.
The prepaid offer avoids false urgency and similar dark patterns covered by the CCPA guidelines.
Phone numbers, addresses and recordings are handled as personal data under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: COD orders for one brand in Hindi and English, with a randomly selected holdout group handled by your current process for comparison.
deliverables: Call script and outcome tags agreed with operations

Pilot report comparing called and holdout orders
Roll-out plan with languages and running cost

what_we_measure.how: Share of COD orders reached within the agreed time after the order was placed.
Delivered, refused and RTO outcomes for called orders compared with the holdout group.
Orders where the address or pincode was corrected, and their delivery outcomes.
Orders converted to prepaid through the UPI link.

faqs.q: How soon after the order does the call happen?
faqs.a: Within the window you choose, usually shortly after the order is placed, while the purchase is fresh in the customer's mind. Orders placed late at night are queued for the next allowed calling hour.
Hindi, English and Hinglish as standard, with regional languages chosen to match your customer mix. The agent can switch language if the customer prefers.

faqs.q: Will a sales pitch put customers off?
faqs.a: The call is short and about their order. A prepaid offer, if you run one, is mentioned once and plainly, without pressure.

faqs.q: How do we know it reduces RTO?
faqs.a: We keep a random holdout group of COD orders that are not called and compare delivery outcomes for both groups. The pilot report shows the comparison, not a projection.
